 Who gets Social Security tomorrow, November 3? Is your payment COLA-adjusted, and how much will beneficiaries receive in November?
 SECTIONS Who gets Social Security tomorrow, November 3? Is your payment COLA-adjusted, and how much will beneficiaries receive in November? By Piyush Shukla , Global Desk Last Updated: Nov 03, 2026, 04:26:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Social Security payments begin November 3 for beneficiaries who started collecting before May 1997. Other recipients will receive benefits on November 10, 18 or 25, depending on their birthdays. Veterans Day shifts the first birthday-based payment forward by a day, while SSI recipients received November's payment early, on October 30, because November 1 falls on Sunday.

 Social Security payments in November 2026: Dates for every group Millions of Americans are set to receive their November Social Security payments , but not everyone will get the money on the same day. The first regular Social Security payments are scheduled to arrive on Tuesday, November 3, while another group has already received its money through the Supplemental Security Income (SSI) programme.
 The payment date depends mainly on when a person first started receiving Social Security benefits. For most people who claimed benefits after May 1997, the date is decided by their birthday. Those who started collecting benefits before that date follow a separate schedule.
November also brings a change to the usual payment calendar. Veterans Day falls on Wednesday, November 11, which affects the payment date for one group of beneficiaries. 
 Who will receive Social Security payments on November 3?
People who started receiving Social Security retirement, disability or survivor benefits before May 1997 are scheduled to receive their November payment on Tuesday, November 3.
This group does not follow the birthday-based payment system used for most other beneficiaries. Instead, the Social Security Administration (SSA) generally sends their payments on the third day of each month.
 Live Events
 For these recipients, November 3 is the first regular Social Security payment date of the month. Anyone who belongs to this group should check their bank account on the scheduled date.
 When will other Social Security beneficiaries receive their November checks?
People who began receiving Social Security benefits after May 1997 are divided into three groups. Their payment dates depend on their dates of birth.
 The usual system assigns payments to the second, third and fourth Wednesday of each month. However, the November calendar is slightly different because the second Wednesday falls on Veterans Day, a federal holiday.
 Here is the complete schedule: 
 November 10: Beneficiaries born between the 1st and 10th of any month will receive their payment one day earlier than the usual second-Wednesday date.
 November 18: People born between the 11th and 20th will receive their November payment.
 November 25: Beneficiaries born between the 21st and 31st will receive their money.
 The November 10 payment is an adjustment to the normal schedule. Since November 11 is a federal holiday, the SSA has moved this group's payment to the previous business day.
 Have SSI recipients already received their November payment?
Yes. SSI follows a different payment calendar from regular Social Security retirement, disability and survivor benefits.
The programme generally sends payments on the first day of each month. However, November 1 falls on a Sunday in 2026. Under the SSA's payment rules, when the scheduled date falls on a weekend or federal holiday, the payment is made on the previous business day.
As a result, SSI recipients were scheduled to receive their November payment on Friday, October 30.
This means the money arrived before the start of November. It is not an additional payment or a bonus. It is the regular November SSI payment issued early because of the calendar.
A payment that does not appear in a bank account on the expected date does not always mean there is a problem with the SSA.
The agency advises beneficiaries to contact their bank or financial institution first. Banks sometimes need additional time to process or display electronic deposits.
If the bank cannot explain the delay, recipients should contact the Social Security Administration to report a missing, late or stolen payment.
The SSA can be reached at 1-800-772-1213 . People who use TTY services can call 1-800-325-0778 .
 Is your November Social Security payment COLA-adjusted?
The November 2026 Social Security payments do not include the 2027 cost-of-living adjustment (COLA). Although the Social Security Administration has announced the new annual increase, beneficiaries will not see the higher amount in their November checks.
The 2027 COLA will take effect with payments issued in January 2027.
 Can working affect your Social Security benefits in 2026?
People who receive Social Security before reaching full retirement age can continue working. However, their earnings may affect how much they receive before reaching that age.
In 2026, beneficiaries who will remain below full retirement age throughout the year can earn up to $24,480 without having benefits withheld under the retirement earnings test.
If their earnings exceed that limit, the SSA withholds $1 in benefits for every $2 earned above the threshold.
This does not mean the withheld money is permanently lost. Once beneficiaries reach full retirement age, the SSA recalculates their payments to account for the months in which benefits were withheld.
It is also important to understand that this earnings test applies to employment income, not ordinary investment income. Dividends, interest and withdrawals from savings generally do not count towards this limit.
